name: Render Motion Graphics (Remotion)
description: Plans the motion-graphics layer with a model, then renders it to overlay segments with alpha using Remotion, carried as QuickTime Animation RGBA (library/tools/overlay_carriage.py). The plan carries its own timebase - an element is timed in timeline seconds and is not tied to a spine block - and several elements may be on screen at once, in rows, composited into one segment. A brand template REFINES the plan by resolving a colour role against its palette; it does not gate the layer. See library/tools/motion_graphics_plan.py.

inputs.name: audio_spine
inputs.description: Timed audio spine for duration and block structure

inputs.name: brand_effect
inputs.description: Brand template effect slots (injected by the pipeline runner). timed_text_overlay declares the text moments rendered for V6. The motion_accents and motion_progress_bar booleans no longer gate the layer - the model plans it; see library/tools/motion_graphics_plan.py.

inputs.name: brand_style
inputs.description: Brand template style slots (injected by the pipeline runner). color_palette REFINES the plan by resolving an entry's colour_role; a project that names no template plans the same layer and states its own colours. See library/tools/brand_palette.py.

inputs.name: creative_direction
inputs.description: Step 2.01's creative direction. Read by the model when it plans the layer: what the piece is doing is what decides whether it wants a title, a quote or nothing at all.

inputs.name: enhancement_spec
inputs.description: The VFX plan from step 4.03, so the overlay layer is planned knowing what the picture treatment is already doing and does not double it.

inputs.name: project_fps
inputs.description: Timebase from the catalog. Every consumer used to read its own 30.0 default because no edge carried it.

inputs.name: project_context
inputs.description: The project's context folder plus the learnings routed to this step, as a MAP the model follows with its shell (never a copy). Injected by the runner from the project's context/ folder and learned_context/ store when this step declares it; a stated absence when the project has neither. Declared here so recorded transcript corrections (read_by *) reach the model that authors motion-graphics copy - measured text arrives corrected through the spine, authored copy only through this. See library/tools/project_context.py.

outputs.name: motion_graphics_overlay
outputs.description: Per-segment overlay paths and metadata for Resolve placement, plus planning_basis - what was proposed, what resolved and every entry that was dropped with its reason.

outputs.name: timed_text_overlay
outputs.description: Rendered timed text segments for the brand template's effect.timed_text_overlay declaration, or declared:false when the template declares none. See library/tools/timed_text_overlay.py.

outputs.name: motion_elements_toon
outputs.description: Bridge output: the motion-graphics roster as a TOON table, one row per element - the table the prompt reads when it plans the layer. Declared here because the bridge emits it on every run and validate_step_output otherwise reports it as an unexpected extra field.

outputs.name: motion_axes_toon
outputs.description: Bridge output: the roster's axes as a TOON table (axis, ranges_over, positions, continuous, resolved_against) - the magnitudes the plan may state per entry. Declared here because the bridge emits it on every run and validate_step_output otherwise reports it as an unexpected extra field.

outputs.name: motion_elements_legend
outputs.description: Bridge output: what each roster column means, carried as DATA because handoff.md is frozen. Declared here because the bridge emits it on every run and validate_step_output otherwise reports it as an unexpected extra field.

outputs.name: timeline_context_toon
outputs.description: Bridge output: the spine as context, one row per block with its span, type and what is said in it - where the speech and cutaways are, not a grid the plan must land on. Declared here because the bridge emits it on every run and validate_step_output otherwise reports it as an unexpected extra field.

outputs.name: motion_graphics_frame
outputs.description: Bridge output: the timebase the plan is timed on - timeline duration, fps, delivery frame, safe area, anchors, entrance/exit characters, colour and type roles, and which elements the renderer draws today. Declared here because the bridge emits it on every run and validate_step_output otherwise reports it as an unexpected extra field.

outputs.name: brand_refinement
outputs.description: Bridge output: what the brand template refines (palette roles, declared effect slots) or that it declares nothing - stated either way, because a silent absence is what used to switch the layer off. Declared here because the bridge emits it on every run and validate_step_output otherwise reports it as an unexpected extra field.

llm_outputs.name: motion_graphics_plan
llm_outputs.description: The motion graphics this video carries. Each entry: element (a key from the roster), anchor, row, copy, color or colour_role, entrance, exit, why. A TIMED entry carries start_seconds and duration_seconds in TIMELINE seconds. An ANCHORED entry instead carries subject (free text saying what the span of speech is about, in your own words), anchor_phrase (words from timeline_context_toon the graphic arrives on) and optionally hold_seconds - and OMITS start_seconds and duration_seconds; naming both timings drops the entry as conflicting_timing. An empty list is a decision that the piece wants none.
